thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT opened — latency spike detected on prod-streaming (SLO: p99 < 800ms). alert: streaming_p99=3.2s, streaming_p95=1.1s, error-rate +3% :rotating_light:

sara: paging eng-oncall (paging rule triggered). @mike you oncall?

mike: oncall here, seeing alert. joining.

aniket: quick snapshot — p95 jumped ~10x across tso routes, p99 dominated by streaming stalls at tail. KV hit rate normal.

jess: customer support reports a few sessions timed out and single-customer calls converting to retries. ticket #C-1289 shows degraded streaming for 10m.

ops-oncall: I'm starting node-level checks. marking suspect pool: gpu-pool-7, node gpu-42.

eng-runtime: logs show repeated ECC correctable errors on gpu-42, plus thermal throttling entries. snippet: ```dmesg | grep -i ecc
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, Multiple correctable ECC errors
Thermal trip: GPU core clock reduced to 750MHz```

mike: nice, can we repro with synthetic? aniket run small load?

aniket: running 5 concurrent long-streams against gpu-42 — I see stalls after ~60s, nvtop shows GPU freq dropping, memory correctables surge. p99 stalls align with ECC bursts.

jess: public-facing fallback engaged? support-bot, post status page note: "degraded streaming for some customers; mitigations in progress"

support-bot: STATUS PAGE updated — incident in progress.

ops-oncall: draining gpu-42 from serving pool now: `kubectl drain node/gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets`

eng-runtime: enabling fallback routing to CPU-backed replicas and smaller model variant (quantized-lite) for streaming routes to keep latency within SLOs. command: `route-policy promote fallback-quantized --scope streaming`

mike: good. set autoscale to allow more small CPU replicas: `hc autoscale set streaming-cpu --min 4 --max 20`

aniket: telemetry after routing change: streaming_p95 -> 210ms, streaming_p99 -> 720ms (much better). tail stalls drop but still occasional 1.2s spikes during drain.

jess: customers A and B notified. CS: "some retries/short disruptions, most sessions recovered with fallback"

ops-oncall: hardware team alerted for gpu-42 ECC/thermal blips. marking node for postmortem and hardware swap.

eng-runtime: mitigation summary: 1) Drain gpu-42 (in progress). 2) Route traffic to quantized fallback. 3) Scale CPU replicas. 4) Short-term: disable KV-prefetch on streaming for affected routes to reduce pressure.

mike: can someone capture nvml logs and save `/var/log/nvml/gpu-42-*.log` to the incident folder?

aniket: uploaded nvml logs and perf traces to \nhttps://internal.redwood/incident/9276543210/artifacts

support-bot: customer impact summary: "~12 customers saw increased latency or short stalls; 2 reported visible session interruptions; no data loss."

incident-bot: SEVERITY set to P2 — partial degradation with mitigation in flight.

jess: handoff — I'll take follow-up with hardware vendor and CS for customer comms. mike, aniket, please add post-incident action items.

mike: noted. action: add stronger node-level ECC alerting (threshold earlier), runbook update to include immediate drain + fallback policy.

aniket: action: automate thermal + ECC correlation dashboard, add NVML traces to our observability pipeline.

ops-oncall: final note: node quarantined for hardware swap, traffic stable on fallback. I'll update when vendor confirms swap window. :white_check_mark:

jess: thanks team. closing live mitigation — leaving monitoring open for 2h and will escalate to RCA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update posted to #incidents thread. next update scheduled in 30m or on status change.
